title: Trying to refine the movement in this game I'm building, which is based on AirGear; what do you think?
author: Intelligent-Basil293
selftext: It's still not as smooth as I'd like, but super happy with the progress so far! Models used; Opus 5-5 and Deepseek flash 4.1

comments.author: speaks-with-stone
comments.body: My first thought at the first frame was "Is that a penis with a backpack?"

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body: Haha, that’s fair; the character model still needs a lot of work. Some of the animations don’t feel right to me yet, and the model is quite basic

comments.author: Tri8ar
comments.body:
Looks sleek, but this isn't something you can properly judge from a video. Only a hands-on playtest can give you the real feel of it: the feedback, the momentum, the camera.

I'd suggest polishing it until you're happy with it, then handing it to someone like a close friend to try. Ideally, watch them play and note where it clicks for them and where they struggle.

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body:
Thanks bud; yep, agreed, it’s hard to judge from a video. 

Will keep working at it and take up ur advice!

comments.author: Traditional-Copy3646
comments.body: Jet Set Radio meet Spiderman? I'd play it. The constant black strokes look cool at first but become annoying quickly though.

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body: Thanks, that’s useful feedback! I was trying to find a way to show velocity; will take that one back to the drawing board

comments.author: anegri
comments.body: I like the look and feel from the video... did you make a mobile version? I think it would be a good phone game

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body: Haven’t made a mobile version; the controls are a bit complicated so not sure how well it would translate to mobile. But will give it some thought and see what’s possible!

replies.author: anegri
replies.body: I feel you, I am refining my controls on a tennis game so that it is easier. [https://anegri.itch.io/battletennis](https://anegri.itch.io/battletennis) this is my first version after porting it to Godot from Unity. What engine did you use?

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body:
Oh this is super fun! smashing the wall is super satisfying :D 

I used Godot; I can't commit a lot of time to this so I picked Godot since it lends itself well to agentic development

replies.author: anegri
replies.body: I think Godot is really nice too coming from Unity, and I switched to gdscript from C# too. How did you specified the post processing on the game? I think mine is a bit plain. Also, I have a soccer game that I tried to publish on crazygames, but has been rejected twice and for the life of I cannot figure out how to get it on there.

comments.author: nicktehbubble
comments.body: Can't see what's going on with the obnoxious popups directly on top of the character model

replies.author: Intelligent-Basil293
replies.body: Fair play; they are a bit obnoxious; will try tweaking them. Thanks for the feedback <3
